what_this_shows: PREREG §1d.5 restart parity, measured on the CURRENT device. The previous receipt was produced by the archived v4cp source (self-declared version=v4) and could not serve as evidence for v5/v6 — independent review round 14, R14-Q5.

identity_sha256.why_they_differ: by construction: the identity sha pins the WINDOW and the LEDGER INPUTS a run actually read, and the resumed run read only the second half. The parity claim is about state_sha256 alone.

state_sha256_covers.state_sha256: the per-symbol material state ONLY — the restart-parity claim is about this number
state_sha256_covers.identity_sha256: device sha, ledger input shas, window, epoch declaration, policy, lot-step source — NOT comparable across a split window
state_sha256_covers.note: a change to ANY per-symbol field changes state_sha256; nothing outside the listed fields is covered by either

boundaries: The parity claim covers the per-symbol material state listed in state_sha256_covers and nothing else.
The online column is UNAVAILABLE for every symbol (order rows store no write time), so `records` are the offline scan's own decisions, not true online receipts.
The epoch is the declared OFFLINE SCAN BASELINE, not a user-signed accounting epoch; carried history is audit state, not settled debt.
A restart across a lot-step change is REFUSED (R14-Q3), so this parity is only claimed within one unit system.
